plan.thinking: First round, nothing measured yet. Key algebraic reading: for symmetric f, max(f*f)=||f||_2^2, so R=||f*f||_2^2/(||f||_1^2||f||_2^2); equivalently R=(∫u^2)/(∫u) with u=(f*f)/max, so R measures how flat/rectangle-like f*f is. Box gives triangular f*f → 2/3 (p0001 confirms). A Gaussian bumps this to 1/√2≈0.707. Sparse delta-combs likely give (2-1/k)/3≤2/3, i.e. worse. So the real lever is a smooth single bump plus direct height optimization. I will put a general randomized height-improver in the deepen slot starting from a Gaussian seed, and use the two explores to scan parametric bump families to learn which shape is extremal.
plan.gist: Round 1: interpret R as flatness of f*f; schedule a general height-improver seeded by a Gaussian (deepen) and two parametric bump-family scans (explore).

beliefs.statement: Constant heights (a single box) give R=2/3 because f*f is triangular.
beliefs.why: reported score 0.666667 for a flat array; matches triangle computation.

beliefs.statement: For symmetric f the peak of f*f is ||f||_2^2, hence R=||f*f||_2^2/(||f||_1^2||f||_2^2)=(∫u^2)/(∫u) with u=(f*f)/max; so R is large exactly when f*f is flat/rectangle-like. A box gives a triangular f*f (R=2/3); a smooth bump gives a flatter-topped f*f, so it should exceed 2/3.
beliefs.refuted_if: a symmetric f whose measured R disagrees with this formula, or a smooth bump scoring below a box.

beliefs.statement: Among compactly supported f the supremum of R is strictly above 2/3 and at least near 1/√2≈0.7071 (Gaussian); likely attained by a smooth single bump, not a rectangle.
beliefs.refuted_if: a broad search showing every single bump stays at or below 2/3, or a construction far above 1/√2.

agenda.question: What single-bump shape maximizes R, and does local search on the height vector from a smooth seed beat 2/3?
agenda.plan: Run a general randomized height-improver seeded with a Gaussian; if it gains, keep deepening (larger N, finer search, flat-top seeds); if it stalls, switch to parametric tuning.
agenda.why: This is the best line (p0001) and the most direct route to a high score.

agenda.question: In the exp-power family f=exp(-|2x-1|^p), which p maximizes R — is the Gaussian (p=2) optimal or do flat-top (p>2) profiles help?
agenda.plan: Grid p, refine around the best, return the best profile; if p>2 wins open a flat-top thread.
agenda.why: Cheaply tests whether flat-topped f*f can beat the Gaussian.

agenda.question: Do other compact bumps (sin^s, (x(1-x))^α, smoothed box) exceed or match the Gaussian's R?
agenda.plan: Score each family across its parameter, report best R and shape; feed the best into future deepens.
agenda.why: Keeps a second, off-best-line source of candidate extremal shapes.

experiments.hypothesis: A Gaussian-like seed plus local height search beats the constant and reaches R≥0.70.
experiments.change: Implement a general improver: if start is None or nearly flat, seed h = exp(-((linspace(-1,1,N=300))/0.33)^2), else h=start.copy(). Then do randomized local refinement on the nonnegative height vector maximizing exact R (recompute via L=[0,*convolve(h,h),0] formula): repeatedly perturb random single indices and small blocks multiplicatively/additively, keep changes that raise R, occasionally accept mild worse moves to escape; loop until process_time()>0.9*budget; return best h. Print best R.
experiments.prediction: Score ~0.70–0.72, clearly above 0.666667.
experiments.if_gain: Deepen: raise N, sharpen search, and test flat-top seeds next.
experiments.if_not: Fall back to analytic exp-power tuning.

experiments.hypothesis: Among f=exp(-|2x-1|^p), p≈2 (Gaussian) is best; p>2 may edge higher via flat-top f*f.
experiments.change: On N=400 sample f=exp(-|2x-1|^p) for x in [0,1]; scan p in {1,1.25,1.5,1.75,2,2.25,2.5,3,4,6}, compute exact R for each, refine best p by ternary search, return the winning profile and print all (p,R).
experiments.prediction: Best R≈0.707 near p=2; report whether any p>2 beats it by >0.001.
experiments.if_gain: If p>2 wins, open a flat-top thread and feed its profile to A1.
experiments.if_not: Record Gaussian as family optimum; stop scanning this family.

experiments.hypothesis: Compact bumps sin^s, (x(1-x))^α, and smoothed box match at best the Gaussian (~1/√2) in their large-parameter limits; none clearly exceeds it.
experiments.change: On N=400 build and score three families by exact R: (a) f=(sin(pi*x))^s for s in {0.5,1,2,4,8}; (b) f=(x*(1-x))^α for α in {0.25,0.5,1,2,4}; (c) box on [0.2,0.8] smoothed by Gaussian of width w in {0.02,0.05,0.1,0.2}. Return the best overall and print all (name,R).
experiments.prediction: Best R near 0.707 (Gaussian-like limits); report if any family exceeds 0.71.
experiments.if_gain: Feed winning profile into A1 deepen searches.
experiments.if_not: Conclude these families do not beat the Gaussian; rely on direct height optimization.

came_back.note: Gained big (0.8034) but far above the predicted 0.70-0.72; note asymmetric peak at 0.562 and 51% zeros.
Flat-top exp-power reached 0.7437, above the predicted ~0.707 — p>2 / flat-top helps.

plan.thinking: Direct height optimization is the dominant lever (0.8078). Two structural clues: every high scorer has an ASYMMETRIC f*f peak (max at 0.324 and 0.562 of support), and flat-top profiles (p0005) beat the Gaussian. Mechanism: by Cauchy-Schwarz max(f*f)=||f||_2^2 only for symmetric f; an asymmetric f lowers ||f*f||_inf while keeping the bulk, which raises R. So the target is an asymmetric, flat-topped f whose f*f is as rectangle-like as possible. This round: (1) a real gradient optimizer (L-BFGS-B) on the p0004 line, (2) an explicit peak-suppression/asymmetry-tilt experiment on p0004, (3) develop the flat-top line from p0005 with direct optimization.
plan.gist: Round 2: asymmetry lowers ||f*f||_inf and flat tops flatten f*f; schedule a gradient optimizer and an asymmetry-tilt experiment on p0004, and a flat-top direct-optimization branch from p0005.

beliefs.statement: For symmetric f the peak of f*f is ||f||_2^2 and R=(∫u^2)/(∫u) with u=(f*f)/max, so R is large when f*f is flat/rectangle-like; but an ASYMMETRIC f has max(f*f)<||f||_2^2 (Cauchy-Schwarz equality needs symmetry), lowering the denominator and raising R when the bulk of f*f is preserved.
beliefs.why: Both top programs have asymmetric f*f peaks (max at 0.324 and 0.562 of support) and score 0.80+.

beliefs.statement: The supremum of R is at least 0.8078, attained by an asymmetric, flat-topped single bump, and lies well above 1/sqrt(2)≈0.7071; the rectangle limit R→1 is unreachable because f*f of nonneg f is continuous and vanishes at the support edges.
beliefs.refuted_if: a broad search showing all asymmetric flat-top bumps saturate below 0.808, or a construction far above 0.81.

beliefs.statement: Direct height-vector optimization from smooth or flat-top seeds reaches R≥0.80, far above any fixed parametric family (best family 0.7437).
beliefs.why: p0004 0.8078 and p0006 0.8034 both come from height optimization, vs 0.7437 for the best parametric family.

agenda.question: Does deliberately lowering ||f*f||_inf via an asymmetric f (peak suppression) raise R beyond 0.8078?
agenda.plan: Apply monotone tilts exp(λ(2x-1)) to the p0004 shape over a λ grid, reoptimize briefly, and plot R vs measured peak; if lower peak correlates with higher R, push asymmetry harder; if not, asymmetry is exhausted.
agenda.why: Top programs are all asymmetric; this tests the mechanism directly.

agenda.question: Does a proper gradient-based optimizer (L-BFGS-B with numerical gradient) beat the crude coordinate/perturbation ascent on the best line?
agenda.plan: Run scipy L-BFGS-B on the height vector from multistarts on the p0004 shape; if it beats 0.8078 keep deepening with higher N, else fall back to structural changes.
agenda.why: p0004's coordinate ascent is inefficient; a real optimizer may find better optima.

experiments.hypothesis: A gradient-based optimizer (L-BFGS-B, numerical gradient) finds a better optimum than coordinate/perturbation ascent on the same line.
experiments.change: In construct, seed from start (p0004 shape). Run scipy.optimize.minimize(method='L-BFGS-B') on the height vector h (N=300, bounds>=0), objective=-R(h) with numerical gradient, from multiple starts: p0004 upsampled, and p0004 multiplied by monotone tilts exp(±λ(2x-1)) for λ in {0.2,0.5,1.0}. Keep the best; spend the remaining budget re-running L-BFGS-B at N=600 from the best. Print R, ||f*f||_inf, ||f||_2^2.
experiments.prediction: Reaches ≥0.81, beating 0.8078.
experiments.if_gain: Keep deepening: higher N and more restarts around the gradient optimum.
experiments.if_not: Gradient no better than coordinate ascent; rely on structural (asymmetry/flat-top) changes.

experiments.hypothesis: Increasing asymmetry lowers ||f*f||_inf and raises R, so a monotone-tilt sweep with re-optimization beats 0.8078.
experiments.change: Start from the p0004 shape h0. For λ in a grid over [-2,2] (say 17 points), form hλ = h0 * exp(λ*(2x-1)), renormalize to max 1, and run a short block-coordinate ascent (blocks of 10, multiplicative+additive, ~2 s each). Record R, ||f*f||_inf, and ||f||_2^2 for each λ; return the best. Print the R-vs-λ and peak-vs-λ curves.
experiments.prediction: Some λ≠0 raises R above 0.8078 and the R-vs-peak curve is monotone decreasing in peak.
experiments.if_gain: Asymmetry is the lever: push tilts further and combine with flat-top seeds.
experiments.if_not: Asymmetry beyond what search already found does not help; drop the peak-suppression thread.

experiments.hypothesis: Direct asymmetric height optimization of a flat-top seed beats the flat-top family's 0.7437 substantially, developing a second line.

experiments.prediction: Reaches ≥0.78 (well above 0.7437, likely below the best line).
experiments.if_gain: Feed the flat-top shape into the best-line deepens; keep the line alive.
experiments.if_not: Flat-top line is weak; park A2.
